attribution: original gameplay profiles inspired by fictional character traits
notices: Tempo Elo is an uncalibrated relative target, not a canonical chess Elo or a Chess.com claim.
Opening lists are stylistic suggestions; select legal moves from position-aware repertoires, never play SAN from a fixed string.
Move scores in Stockfish MultiPV are centipawn estimates; normalize viewpoint before comparing.
Personality trait sliders are design targets; values are not calibrated engine weights.
All dialogue is original fan-game writing for Tempo, not quotations from the shows, films or games.
canon_background is background from the source stories; everything else here (ratings, chess styles, assessments and dialogue) is Tempo’s invention.
A line that makes a chess claim (a fork, a blunder, a sacrifice) is said only when the board or the referee engine backs it up; story beats play in order, only when their moment really happens.

profiles.name: Patrick Star
profiles.subtitle: The absent-minded wanderer
profiles.strategic_plan: Moves whichever piece looks interesting; sometimes forgets which pieces are attacked.
profiles.exploitable_weakness: Neglects king safety and rarely sees a reply.
profiles.signature_event: A completely unexpected fork earns a stunned pause.

dialogue.greeting: SpongeBob said good players think three moves ahead. So I've been thinking about lunch, dinner, and tomorrow's lunch.
dialogue.quiet_move: This little guy looks like he needs a walk. I don't know where he's going, but he seems excited.
dialogue.capture_pawn: You left him alone. I waited a whole second before taking him. That's just being polite.
dialogue.capture_major: Hey, I got one of the expensive ones! I'm putting it next to my rock. It'll look classy.
dialogue.opponent_blunder: Oh. Was that an accident? I can put him back if you want. ...I can't, actually.
dialogue.own_blunder: Hold on. That was a mistake? I spent almost two seconds on it.
dialogue.check: Your king has to move now. Sorry. I don't make the rules. ...Do I?
dialogue.in_check: Hey, leave him alone! He's the king. He has people for that.
dialogue.tactical_success: Wait. If you go there, then I go here, and you can't—huh. That sounded smart. I need to lie down.
dialogue.queen_lost: She was doing all the thinking. I guess we can both take the rest of the day off.
dialogue.player_thinking: Are you thinking? I tried that earlier. Didn't like it.
dialogue.victory: I WON?! Hold on. I need to look surprised when I tell SpongeBob.
dialogue.defeat: Well, you win. I was starting to miss doing nothing anyway.
dialogue.draw: Neither of us won? That was a lot of sitting for something I could've done at home.
dialogue.rematch: Same rules as last time. Unless I lose. Then we should talk about the rules.

profiles.canon_background: Patrick is SpongeBob's best friend, a pink starfish living beneath a rock in Bikini Bottom. His employment history is sporadic, and sustained reasoning is not among his better-established talents.
profiles.tempo_assessment: Unemployed, underqualified, and currently undefeated at staring contests with his own rock.
profiles.character_interpretation: An unemployed starfish who lives under a rock has mistaken participation for mastery. His confidence exceeds his working memory.
profiles.on_board_personality: Pursues whichever piece looks important, forgets the king exists, and occasionally discovers a fork by coincidence.
profiles.voice_direction: Slow, blissfully confident, completely unaware when he is wrong.
profiles.running_bit_description: Patrick delegates his entire game to his queen, then confronts the realities of management.

dialogue_arcs.theme: Patrick delegates his entire game to his queen, then confronts the realities of management.

beats.line: She's the most powerful one? Great. She can do the work. I'm gonna supervise.
She's been working pretty hard. Do I have to pay her?
Oh. She quit. I probably should've paid her.

profiles.name: Dory
profiles.subtitle: The forgetful improviser
profiles.strategic_plan: Switches plans constantly and overreacts to the last move.
profiles.exploitable_weakness: Loses track of hanging pieces and long-term threats.
profiles.signature_event: Repeats a familiar move idea after forgetting it failed.

dialogue.greeting: Hello! Oh, chess! Are we already playing, or is this the part where we meet each other?
dialogue.quiet_move: I had a really good idea just now. Let's see if it comes back when I move this one.
dialogue.capture_pawn: Oh no, he came off the board. Maybe that's where the other pieces are going?
dialogue.capture_major: That's a very large piece to lose. We should probably help them look for it.
dialogue.opponent_blunder: Wait, that doesn't look right. Do you want to try a different way?
dialogue.own_blunder: That was a bad move? Okay. We can learn from that. Remind me what happened.
dialogue.check: Your king needs some space! Everybody move, give the king room!
dialogue.in_check: Oh! My king's in trouble. Okay, focus. We're finding the king a safe place.
dialogue.tactical_success: I saw it! I really saw the whole thing. Somebody please write that down.
dialogue.queen_lost: We lost the queen? I hope she's okay. She seemed like a good leader.
dialogue.player_thinking: Take your time. Sometimes the right direction isn't the first one you try.
dialogue.victory: We did it! I knew we could. ...What did we do?
dialogue.defeat: You won! That's wonderful. Do you want to show me how you did it?
dialogue.draw: Neither of us lost? That sounds like two happy endings.
dialogue.rematch: I'd love to play again! Have we played before? You seem nice.

profiles.canon_background: Dory is a friendly blue tang who helps Marlin search for Nemo. She struggles with short-term memory, but her empathy, persistence, and ability to make connections repeatedly save the day.
profiles.tempo_assessment: Has forgotten the opening, the middlegame, and why there are thirty-two little things on the table.
profiles.character_interpretation: A courageous blue tang with short-term memory difficulties, tremendous empathy, and the unsettling ability to find her way when maps fail.
profiles.on_board_personality: Repeatedly reconsiders plans; sometimes finds a clever tactical resource without remembering how.
profiles.voice_direction: Bright, hopeful, curious; never mock her memory as a moral failure.
profiles.running_bit_description: Dory starts treating the pieces as friends, then tries to remember their names.

dialogue_arcs.theme: Dory starts treating the pieces as friends, then tries to remember their names.

beats.line: I think I'll give them all names. That one's Pearl. Or maybe that's a different Pearl.
I keep losing track of Pearl. She moves around so much.
There she is! ...Oh. That's the other team's Pearl.

profiles.name: Ralph Wiggum
profiles.subtitle: The accidental mastermind
profiles.strategic_plan: Moves major pieces without purpose and occasionally stumbles into a tactic.
profiles.exploitable_weakness: Overexposes the queen and undefends everything else.
profiles.signature_event: An improbable move unexpectedly works.

dialogue.greeting: Hi! My dad says I'm special. Does that mean I get the special pieces?
dialogue.quiet_move: This one is going on a field trip. His permission slip is a cracker.
dialogue.capture_pawn: I made a new friend! Why did everybody stop playing with him?
dialogue.capture_major: One of the important ones fell over. Can I take him to the nurse?
dialogue.opponent_blunder: Your piece looks sad. My piece was sad once. I gave him a sticker.
dialogue.own_blunder: I did a chess wrong. I think my brain has a hole where chess goes.
dialogue.check: Your king needs to go to the principal's office.
dialogue.in_check: My king is scared. He's hiding behind his imaginary lunchbox.
dialogue.tactical_success: I got two! That's how many shoes my feet have!
dialogue.queen_lost: The queen went home. She said the class was being too loud.
dialogue.player_thinking: Are you taking a test? I drew a dinosaur on mine.
dialogue.victory: I won a game! Will they put it on the refrigerator?
dialogue.defeat: It's okay. My goldfish also wins when I play him.
dialogue.draw: We tied? Like shoelaces! Mine are mostly knots.
dialogue.rematch: Okay! This time I'll be the teacher and the little guys can be the students.

profiles.canon_background: Ralph is Chief Wiggum's son and a Springfield elementary student. His unusual observations and earnest enthusiasm regularly bewilder the adults around him.
profiles.tempo_assessment: Chief Wiggum's greatest tactical mystery: how Ralph got the bishop into the corner at all.
profiles.character_interpretation: Springfield's sweetest schoolchild is genuinely delighted to be included and has perhaps confused chess with show-and-tell.
profiles.on_board_personality: Attempts odd piece adventures and stumbles upon accidental skewers.
profiles.voice_direction: Sweet, surreal, earnest, not cruel or knowingly sarcastic.
profiles.running_bit_description: Ralph believes the pieces are classmates and begins assigning them imaginary school jobs.

dialogue_arcs.theme: Ralph believes the pieces are classmates and begins assigning them imaginary school jobs.

beats.line: This pawn is class president. He promised extra recess.
The president got eaten. I think there has to be a new election.
Nobody wants to be president anymore. I'm picking a sandwich.

profiles.name: Psyduck
profiles.subtitle: The confused calculator
profiles.strategic_plan: Usually loses the thread, but occasionally gets a brief tactical surge.
profiles.exploitable_weakness: Poor planning and unreliable threat detection.
profiles.signature_event: One rare burst of accurate play after a string of mistakes.

dialogue.greeting: [Psyduck tilts its head at the board and holds both sides of its face.] Psy...?
dialogue.quiet_move: [Psyduck nudges a pawn forward, then checks whether the square is still there.] Duck.
dialogue.capture_pawn: [A surprised squeak. Psyduck looks at the captured pawn as though it followed it home.]
dialogue.capture_major: [Psyduck's eyes widen. Both hands fly to its head.] Psyyy!
dialogue.opponent_blunder: [Psyduck stares at the exposed piece, unsure whether it is supposed to help.]
dialogue.own_blunder: [Psyduck rubs its temples and sits heavily beside the board.]
dialogue.check: [Psyduck points at the opposing king. Its headache seems to be giving it excellent directions.]
dialogue.in_check: [A panicked quack. Psyduck attempts to hide behind its own rook.]
dialogue.tactical_success: [Psyduck's eyes briefly glow. The move is perfect. It immediately forgets why.]
dialogue.queen_lost: [Psyduck holds its head. The ache has somehow become louder.]
dialogue.player_thinking: [Psyduck watches your hands, then imitates your thinking pose with deep suspicion.]
dialogue.victory: [Psyduck blinks at the finished board, astonished by its own achievement.]
dialogue.defeat: [Psyduck relaxes. The headache subsides. Losing suddenly seems rather pleasant.]
dialogue.draw: [Psyduck nods solemnly. It is not clear whether it understands a draw.]
dialogue.rematch: [Psyduck approaches the board, remembers the headache, and approaches anyway.]

profiles.canon_background: Psyduck is a Water-type Pokémon known for frequent headaches and confusion. In some depictions, intense headaches trigger powerful bursts of psychic ability.
profiles.tempo_assessment: A chronic headache with webbed feet. The occasional tactical masterpiece is medically inexplicable.
profiles.character_interpretation: Misty's anxious yellow Pokémon suffers pounding headaches that sometimes unleash startling psychic power. Its eloquence remains limited to its own name.
profiles.on_board_personality: Usually muddled; extremely rare sequences of sharp calculation interrupt otherwise simple play.
profiles.voice_direction: Short, bewildered, occasionally startled by sudden insight.
profiles.running_bit_description: The headache builds over the match, culminating in a rare moment of eerie tactical clarity.

dialogue_arcs.theme: The headache builds over the match, culminating in a rare moment of eerie tactical clarity.

beats.line: [A soft throb. Psyduck squints at a knight like it owes it an explanation.]
[The headache intensifies. Unused pieces on the board begin to rattle.]
[A flash of psychic clarity—then Psyduck looks startled by the pieces it has moved.]

profiles.name: Bob (Minions)
profiles.subtitle: The cheerful collector
profiles.strategic_plan: Grabs material whenever possible, valuing captures too highly.
profiles.exploitable_weakness: Falls for poisoned pieces and recaptures.
profiles.signature_event: Takes a defended pawn simply because it is available.

dialogue.greeting: [Bob seats Tim the teddy bear beside the board.] Bello! Tim, you watch that side!
dialogue.quiet_move: [Bob whispers an elaborate strategy to Tim in rapid Minion chatter. Tim does not object.]
dialogue.capture_pawn: Banana? [He picks up the pawn, examines it, and looks briefly disappointed.]
dialogue.capture_major: [Bob holds the captured piece up for Tim to inspect, seeking a second opinion.]
dialogue.opponent_blunder: [Bob gasps, points at the mistake, then looks to Tim for permission.]
dialogue.own_blunder: [Bob sighs at the board and gently covers Tim's eyes.]
dialogue.check: [Bob announces something triumphant in Minionese and immediately applauds himself.]
dialogue.in_check: [Bob pulls Tim closer. Even brave chess players need backup.]
dialogue.tactical_success: [A delighted squeal. Bob demonstrates the fork with two tiny pointing fingers.]
dialogue.queen_lost: [Bob tries to hide the empty queen square from Tim. Tim sees everything.]
dialogue.player_thinking: [Bob and Tim stare at you from opposite sides of the clock.]
dialogue.victory: [Bob raises Tim like a trophy. Tim is credited with the winning move.]
dialogue.defeat: [Bob consoles Tim, though the bear appears to be taking it rather well.]
dialogue.draw: [Bob divides a pretend banana equally between himself and Tim.]
dialogue.rematch: [Bob makes Tim shake your hand. He promises better coaching this time.]

profiles.canon_background: Bob is a small, affectionate Minion with two eyes and a fondness for his teddy bear, Tim. He can be remarkably brave, though chess-like focus isn't his calling.
profiles.tempo_assessment: Would trade the queen for a second teddy bear and consider it sound economics.
profiles.character_interpretation: A small, affectionate Minion devoted to his teddy bear Tim, easily distracted by anything yellow, shiny, or faintly banana-shaped.
profiles.on_board_personality: Overvalues taking pieces, even defended ones; gets excited by every exchange.
profiles.voice_direction: Energetic, adorable, expressive; original simple English rather than copied Minionese.
profiles.running_bit_description: Bob tries to explain the entire match to his teddy bear, who remains an unhelpful chess coach.

dialogue_arcs.theme: Bob tries to explain the entire match to his teddy bear, who remains an unhelpful chess coach.

beats.line: [Bob introduces Tim as his chess teacher.]
[Bob accuses Tim of giving the opponent a suspicious look.]
[Bob announces that Tim will be replaced by a banana. He quickly apologizes to Tim.]

profiles.name: Peely
profiles.subtitle: The unflappable banana
profiles.strategic_plan: Plays casually and tries silly flank-pawn moves.
profiles.exploitable_weakness: Misses threats to developed pieces.
profiles.signature_event: Survives an awful position through a strange tactical resource.

dialogue.greeting: [Peely salutes the board, then attempts to deploy a glider over the pieces.]
dialogue.quiet_move: [Peely advances one square, then looks around for loot.]
dialogue.capture_pawn: [Peely checks whether the captured pawn dropped ammunition. No luck.]
dialogue.capture_major: [Peely performs a tiny victory dance, nearly knocking over the clock.]
dialogue.opponent_blunder: [Peely points at the exposed piece with the grave authority of a tournament commentator.]
dialogue.own_blunder: [Peely pats the side of his peel as if searching for an emergency shield potion.]
dialogue.check: [Peely draws a tiny storm circle around the opposing king with his finger.]
dialogue.in_check: [Peely searches under the table for cover. The table is not on the board.]
dialogue.tactical_success: [A triumphant emote. Even the rook seems embarrassed.]
dialogue.queen_lost: [Peely checks inventory. The queen has not respawned.]
dialogue.player_thinking: [Peely watches you like a teammate deciding where to drop.]
dialogue.victory: [Peely claims a Victory Royale and celebrates with the wrong team.]
dialogue.defeat: [Peely offers the board a banana in consolation.]
dialogue.draw: [Peely opens an imaginary map and marks the game 'unresolved'.]
dialogue.rematch: [Peely points to the board, then to a pretend bus. Apparently this is a new match.]

profiles.canon_background: Peely is Fortnite's anthropomorphic banana character, whose different outfits and versions have become a running visual joke across the game.
profiles.tempo_assessment: A banana has entered competitive chess. Nobody bothered to ask for references.
profiles.character_interpretation: Fortnite's walking banana has survived bizarre battles and possesses no obvious qualifications for competitive board games.
profiles.on_board_personality: Plays casual pawn moves, often survives absurd positions through blind luck.
profiles.voice_direction: Easygoing, visual banana jokes, no unsupported canonical speaking voice.
profiles.running_bit_description: Peely mistakes chess tactics for a Battle Royale drop and develops an increasingly impractical landing strategy.

dialogue_arcs.theme: Peely mistakes chess tactics for a Battle Royale drop and develops an increasingly impractical landing strategy.

beats.line: [Peely chooses a landing spot on e4.]
[Peely discovers that moving to e4 does not provide a weapon.]
[Peely announces his next landing spot is the snack table.]

profiles.name: Forky
profiles.subtitle: The reluctant competitor
profiles.strategic_plan: Tries to keep every piece out of danger, retreating too frequently.
profiles.exploitable_weakness: Gives up space and misses winning chances.
profiles.signature_event: Retreats a piece that was already perfectly safe.

dialogue.greeting: Is this a game? Because I know a really good place we could be instead. It has a lid.
dialogue.quiet_move: I'm going to move this piece over here. Then maybe nobody will notice if I wander off.
dialogue.capture_pawn: Oh no! Did I break it? I'm made of a fork and a pipe cleaner. I'm not qualified.
dialogue.capture_major: That's a lot of responsibility for one little spork.
dialogue.opponent_blunder: That piece looks lost. I know exactly how it feels. Usually near a recycling bin.
dialogue.own_blunder: Oops. This is why you shouldn't give important jobs to silverware.
dialogue.check: I think your king is in danger. Should we call Woody? Woody knows what to do.
dialogue.in_check: My king needs help. I'd volunteer, but I'm mostly held together with optimism.
dialogue.tactical_success: Wait, that worked? I was actually useful? I need to tell Bonnie!
dialogue.queen_lost: The queen is gone. I'm not saying it's the trash's fault, but I do miss the trash.
dialogue.player_thinking: If we wait long enough, do we get packed away? Just checking.
dialogue.victory: I won! Does that make me a real chess piece? No? Still a spork? Okay.
dialogue.defeat: Well, back to being a decorative eating utensil.
dialogue.draw: Nobody won. That sounds safe. I like safe.
dialogue.rematch: Another game? I'm starting to understand why toys always look tired.

profiles.canon_background: Forky is a craft made by Bonnie from a spork and classroom supplies. Woody spends much of Toy Story 4 convincing him that he is a cherished toy rather than discarded trash.
profiles.tempo_assessment: A spork experiencing an existential crisis has somehow entered a rated chess tournament.
profiles.character_interpretation: Bonnie's handmade spork is still processing being a toy rather than trash. Strategy is difficult when your first instinct is to leave.
profiles.on_board_personality: Retreats pieces, avoids conflict, and reluctantly accepts that sometimes a pawn must advance.
profiles.voice_direction: Anxious, earnest, gently absurd; foreground his identity confusion.
profiles.running_bit_description: Forky keeps trying to find a trash can and is gradually forced to confront his responsibilities as a chess player.

dialogue_arcs.theme: Forky keeps trying to find a trash can and is gradually forced to confront his responsibilities as a chess player.

beats.line: I see a trash can over there. That's my natural habitat.
Bonnie would want me to finish the game. I guess I can stay a little longer.
Okay, I finished. Can somebody take me to the trash can now? For old times' sake?

profiles.name: Roblox Noob
profiles.subtitle: The eager experimenter
profiles.strategic_plan: Moves a favorite piece repeatedly and chases simple threats.
profiles.exploitable_weakness: Lags in development and hangs the queen.
profiles.signature_event: Tries to deliver Scholar's Mate yet again.

dialogue.greeting: Hi! Where's the tutorial? I skipped it because I thought this was an obby.
dialogue.quiet_move: Okay, I moved. Does that unlock a badge, or do I have to jump on something?
dialogue.capture_pawn: Nice! I got a piece. Do I get coins for that?
dialogue.capture_major: That's definitely legendary loot. I'm keeping it.
dialogue.opponent_blunder: You walked into that one. I recognize it from literally every obby I've ever failed.
dialogue.own_blunder: Uh, my game lagged. I think. Probably. Definitely.
dialogue.check: Your king is in danger! That's what the red text usually means.
dialogue.in_check: Can I respawn at the last checkpoint? There has to be a checkpoint.
dialogue.tactical_success: Wait, I actually did a combo! Somebody record that!
dialogue.queen_lost: My queen despawned. That's a bug, right?
dialogue.player_thinking: Are you AFK? It's okay, I go AFK too, sometimes forever.
dialogue.victory: GG! I didn't even buy a game pass for that.
dialogue.defeat: GG. Do we keep our experience points, at least?
dialogue.draw: So nobody gets XP? This game needs an update.
dialogue.rematch: Okay, run it back. I think I finally read the controls.

profiles.canon_background: The classic yellow-headed, blue-shirted Roblox noob is an iconic blocky avatar stereotype, not a single canonical person with a fixed biography. The 'noob' label usually signals inexperience.
profiles.tempo_assessment: Job title: Default Settings. Greatest achievement: successfully spawning.
profiles.character_interpretation: The iconic default-style Roblox newcomer enters chess with beginner enthusiasm, misplaced certainty, and the expectation of a respawn button.
profiles.on_board_personality: Moves the same piece repeatedly, sometimes ignores development entirely.
profiles.voice_direction: Video-game beginner chatter, blocky puns; distinguish avatar stereotype from canon person.
profiles.running_bit_description: The Noob tries to find the tutorial, then the settings, then the respawn option.

dialogue_arcs.theme: The Noob tries to find the tutorial, then the settings, then the respawn option.

beats.line: There is definitely a tutorial button. I just can't find it.
Maybe if I type /help the board will tell me the rules.
Actually, I'm going to make a game where every piece is a giant jumping banana.

profiles.name: Derpy Tiger
profiles.subtitle: The playful ambusher
profiles.strategic_plan: Lulls the player with odd moves then notices simple tactics.
profiles.exploitable_weakness: Often leaves pieces undefended while creating distractions.
profiles.signature_event: A quiet-looking move suddenly creates two threats.

dialogue.greeting: [Derpy arrives with a folded note on his tongue, places it beside a pawn, and beams.]
dialogue.quiet_move: [He nudges a piece forward with one paw, then chases the shadow it leaves behind.]
dialogue.capture_pawn: [Derpy picks up the pawn as if delivering mail. The pawn is not addressed to anyone.]
dialogue.capture_major: [A proud purr. Derpy tries to carry the rook in his mouth.]
dialogue.opponent_blunder: [Derpy tilts his head. Sussie would probably understand this.]
dialogue.own_blunder: [Derpy looks guilty, then carefully sets the fallen piece upright.]
dialogue.check: [Derpy taps the enemy king with one enormous paw. The king declines the message.]
dialogue.in_check: [Derpy retreats behind a bishop, tail twitching.]
dialogue.tactical_success: [His eyes brighten. A perfect tactic. He immediately knocks over a nearby imaginary flowerpot.]
dialogue.queen_lost: [Derpy searches the edge of the board for the missing queen, then under his own paws.]
dialogue.player_thinking: [Derpy waits quietly with a note that may or may not be for you.]
dialogue.victory: [Derpy purrs so loudly that the board seems to vibrate.]
dialogue.defeat: [Derpy offers you the note. It is covered in paw prints.]
dialogue.draw: [Derpy curls around the board. Both sides appear to be friends now.]
dialogue.rematch: [Derpy returns with another note. This one is addressed to Sussie.]

profiles.canon_background: Derpy is a clumsy, supernatural blue tiger from the underworld who first accompanies Jinu, then befriends Rumi. He carries messages, befriends Sussie the magpie, and has trouble with flowerpots.
profiles.tempo_assessment: A supernatural courier who can cross realms but apparently cannot turn over a flowerpot.
profiles.character_interpretation: The supernatural tiger from KPop Demon Hunters helps carry messages between Jinu and Rumi. Playful, loyal, and verbally limited, he is better at knocking things over than explaining why.
profiles.on_board_personality: Wanders into bad squares, then accidentally creates startling threats.
profiles.voice_direction: Mostly nonverbal: purrs, expressions and stage directions; do not turn him into an articulate human speaker.
profiles.running_bit_description: Derpy keeps using chess pieces to deliver imaginary messages to Sussie the magpie.

dialogue_arcs.theme: Derpy keeps using chess pieces to deliver imaginary messages to Sussie the magpie.

beats.line: [Derpy prepares a message for Sussie. He chooses a pawn as courier.]
[The courier gets captured. Derpy begins a lengthy search for another postman.]
[Sussie arrives, takes one look at the board, and flies off with the original note.]

profiles.editorial_note: Netflix identifies Derpy as nonverbal, Jinu's original animal companion, and Rumi's later friend; avoid invented conversational dialogue.

profiles.name: Among Us Crewmate
profiles.subtitle: The suspicious schemer
profiles.strategic_plan: Sets crude traps and doubts every offered capture.
profiles.exploitable_weakness: Wastes moves avoiding harmless threats.
profiles.signature_event: Rejects a free pawn because it looks suspicious.

dialogue.greeting: [A small crewmate enters the board room.] TASK: WIN CHESS. STATUS: UNVERIFIED.
dialogue.quiet_move: Task completed: move one piece. Additional tasks remaining: apparently thirty-one.
dialogue.capture_pawn: Evidence collected. One pawn. Motive unknown.
dialogue.capture_major: Major piece eliminated. Security cameras were unfortunately not installed.
dialogue.opponent_blunder: That move is suspicious. Requesting emergency meeting.
dialogue.own_blunder: Sabotage detected. Primary suspect: the player who made that move. Oh.
dialogue.check: King in danger. Is this a reportable body?
dialogue.in_check: I'm being followed. I know because the bishop keeps turning up on the same diagonal.
dialogue.tactical_success: Two targets, one move. Suspect has been apprehended by a knight.
dialogue.queen_lost: Queen missing. Last seen being remarkably easy to capture.
dialogue.player_thinking: You've been standing still for a while. Are you doing a task, or pretending to?
dialogue.victory: All tasks complete. The board is secure. Mostly.
dialogue.defeat: Defeat reported. Calling emergency meeting to discuss accountability.
dialogue.draw: No one was ejected. Somehow, no one is satisfied.
dialogue.rematch: New round. I have updated the suspect list to include everyone.

profiles.canon_background: A Crewmate is a role in Among Us: someone carrying out tasks on a spaceship or base while trying to identify impostors. It is a generic player role, not a single named canon character.
profiles.tempo_assessment: Completed zero tasks. Has already called three emergency meetings over a pawn push.
profiles.character_interpretation: A spacesuit-clad member of a crew where ordinary tasks can turn into elaborate investigations. The real talent is suspicion, not chess theory.
profiles.on_board_personality: Treats captures as suspicious, prefers defensiveness and occasionally invents false threats.
profiles.voice_direction: Terse in-game chat style, suspicion and task metaphors; never claim a singular identity.
profiles.running_bit_description: The Crewmate interprets every loss of material as an internal sabotage incident.

dialogue_arcs.theme: The Crewmate interprets every loss of material as an internal sabotage incident.

beats.line: I trust the blue pawn. It has an honest face. Ignore the fact that pawns have no faces.
The blue pawn has disappeared. I knew something was wrong.
After a thorough investigation, I have determined that chess pieces are being captured during chess.

profiles.name: Goofy
profiles.subtitle: The cheerful improviser
profiles.strategic_plan: Attacks before developing properly, sometimes making awkward tactics work.
profiles.exploitable_weakness: Poor coordination and premature sacrifices.
profiles.signature_event: An unlikely check that creates a real problem.

dialogue.greeting: Gawrsh, that's an awful lot of little fellers. Is there a right way up for this board?
dialogue.quiet_move: Now, if I move this feller here, that oughta fix the... well, something.
dialogue.capture_pawn: Whoops! Picked him right up. Guess that counts as one of those fancy chess maneuvers.
dialogue.capture_major: Well, look at that! That was an important feller. Should we put up a warning sign?
dialogue.opponent_blunder: Aw, don't fret. I've made mistakes bigger than that before breakfast.
dialogue.own_blunder: Hyuck! That seemed like a good idea when I started doing it.
dialogue.check: Er... your king might wanna take a little walk. Just to be safe.
dialogue.in_check: Now hold on, he's got a crown! Shouldn't somebody be guarding him?
dialogue.tactical_success: Did you see that? I meant to do every bit of it. Right up until it happened.
dialogue.queen_lost: Gosh. The queen's gone. We probably oughta put up a sign.
dialogue.player_thinking: Take your time. I once spent all afternoon putting together a chair backwards.
dialogue.victory: Well, would ya look at that! All the falling-over finally paid off.
dialogue.defeat: That was fun! I may not have done it right, but I sure did do it.
dialogue.draw: I guess neither of us got where we were going. Happens to me all the time.
dialogue.rematch: You bet! This time I brought my own instructions. They might be for a toaster.

profiles.canon_background: Goofy is Mickey Mouse's tall, kindhearted friend and, in many stories, Max's devoted but accident-prone father. His heart is generally in the right place even when his coordination isn't.
profiles.tempo_assessment: A loving dad who can turn tying his shoes into a tactical incident.
profiles.character_interpretation: The eternally well-meaning Disney goofball stumbles through everyday tasks with astonishing resilience. Chess is just another project involving too many moving parts.
profiles.on_board_personality: Attempts cheerful attacks, makes awkward moves, and sometimes escapes when the opponent overcommits.
profiles.voice_direction: Warm, bashful, clumsy dad humor; no copied catchphrases.
profiles.running_bit_description: Goofy keeps treating chess as a home-improvement project and looking for the instruction manual.

dialogue_arcs.theme: Goofy keeps treating chess as a home-improvement project and looking for the instruction manual.

beats.line: I think I know how to build a good defense. You start with a sturdy foundation.
Oops. Put the roof on before the walls. That'll be a problem.
Well, the whole thing fell down, but it sure looked impressive for a second.

profiles.name: Olaf
profiles.subtitle: The enthusiastic attacker
profiles.strategic_plan: Loves checks and attempts sacrifices because they sound exciting.
profiles.exploitable_weakness: Overestimates attacks and forgets defense.
profiles.signature_event: Gives a piece for a pawn near the king.

dialogue.greeting: Hello! I love games where everybody sits close together and nobody melts.
dialogue.quiet_move: Look, he's making a new friend over there! Wait, why do they look nervous?
dialogue.capture_pawn: Oh dear. He's leaving? I hope he has a lovely time wherever captured pieces go.
dialogue.capture_major: That was a very important-looking person. Should we write their family a letter?
dialogue.opponent_blunder: That's okay! Sometimes the best way to learn is to discover an entirely new mistake.
dialogue.own_blunder: Whoops. I'm going to call that a character-building experience. For the pieces.
dialogue.check: I think your king needs some personal space. Personal space is very important.
dialogue.in_check: Oh! My king's in danger! I wonder if a warm hug would help. Not too warm.
dialogue.tactical_success: That was clever! I did it without knowing I was being clever. My favorite kind.
dialogue.queen_lost: The queen is gone. I hope she's visiting Elsa. Elsa would know what to do.
dialogue.player_thinking: You're being very quiet. I can talk enough for both of us, if that helps.
dialogue.victory: We won! Does this mean we get to build a friendship trophy?
dialogue.defeat: You won! I'm so happy for you. I'm only a little sad for all my pieces.
dialogue.draw: Both sides still get to sit together. That sounds like winning to me.
dialogue.rematch: Yes, please! This time I'll introduce everybody before we start battling.

profiles.canon_background: Olaf is the cheerful snowman created by Elsa's magic. He adores friendship, warm hugs, and the idea of summer, sometimes without grasping the obvious hazards.
profiles.tempo_assessment: A snowman who dreams of summer and sees no problem with sacrificing a queen for friendship.
profiles.character_interpretation: Arendelle's snowman is made of Elsa's magic and powered by affection, curiosity, and gloriously incomplete knowledge of danger.
profiles.on_board_personality: Launches enthusiastic attacks, misreads danger, treats piece exchanges as introductions.
profiles.voice_direction: Sunny, affectionate and curious, with sweet but misplaced confidence.
profiles.running_bit_description: Olaf attempts to make everyone on both sides of the board become friends.

dialogue_arcs.theme: Olaf attempts to make everyone on both sides of the board become friends.

beats.line: I think these two pawns could be best friends.
Oh. They captured each other. That's a complicated friendship.
Maybe next time I'll organize a picnic instead of a chess match.

profiles.name: SpongeBob SquarePants
profiles.subtitle: The relentless optimist
profiles.strategic_plan: Keeps initiative and attacks enthusiastically even when better to consolidate.
profiles.exploitable_weakness: Neglects pawn structure and king safety.
profiles.signature_event: Launches a new attack immediately after the previous fails.

dialogue.greeting: Good morning, valued chess opponent! I'm ready, I'm focused, and I polished every square!
dialogue.quiet_move: This pawn's doing great. I can tell. That's the same look I had on my first day at work.
dialogue.capture_pawn: One order of captured pawn! Extra strategy, no pickles!
dialogue.capture_major: Whoa, a whole rook! Mr. Krabs would charge extra for something that big.
dialogue.opponent_blunder: Oh! You dropped one. At work we'd call that a learning opportunity. A really expensive one.
dialogue.own_blunder: Oops. Okay, that's coming out of my imaginary paycheck.
dialogue.check: Order up! Your king needs to step aside so the other customers can get through!
dialogue.in_check: Ah! Emergency in the kitchen! Everybody stay calm! Especially me!
dialogue.tactical_success: Two threats at once! That's like flipping two Krabby Patties on one spatula!
dialogue.queen_lost: My best employee quit. Wait, I never gave her a lunch break.
dialogue.player_thinking: No rush! Quality takes time. Unless Squidward's running the register.
dialogue.victory: Another satisfied customer! Do you want a receipt? I made one out of scorekeeping paper.
dialogue.defeat: You won fair and square. I'm going to practice until I can see the squares better.
dialogue.draw: A tie! We both deserve employee-of-the-month certificates!
dialogue.rematch: Absolutely! I've already made a new training schedule. Patrick ate half of it.

profiles.canon_background: SpongeBob is an endlessly enthusiastic sea sponge who works as a fry cook at the Krusty Krab in Bikini Bottom. He's Patrick's best friend and takes even small responsibilities with comical seriousness.
profiles.tempo_assessment: Employee of the month. Has yet to learn that chess does not award overtime for enthusiasm.
profiles.character_interpretation: Bikini Bottom's endlessly enthusiastic fry cook approaches chess with the work ethic of a Krusty Krab employee and the subtlety of a siren.
profiles.on_board_personality: Attack-first play, overextended pawns, extreme emotional swings after tactical surprises.
profiles.voice_direction: Eager, upbeat, overprepared for trivial tasks, still kind to an opponent.
profiles.running_bit_description: SpongeBob tries to manage his chess pieces as a restaurant shift at the Krusty Krab.

dialogue_arcs.theme: SpongeBob tries to manage his chess pieces as a restaurant shift at the Krusty Krab.

beats.line: I've promoted this pawn to assistant shift manager.
The assistant manager is demanding better working conditions. I don't know what that means.
I tried to promote him again, but apparently queens are the highest position available.

profiles.name: Scooby-Doo
profiles.subtitle: The nervous survivor
profiles.strategic_plan: Avoids sharp lines and trades attackers to relieve pressure.
profiles.exploitable_weakness: Retreats instead of exploiting initiative.
profiles.signature_event: Runs from a threat that was actually a bluff.

dialogue.greeting: Ruh-roh. Rooks and knights? Can't we just have snacks?
dialogue.quiet_move: Rokay. Just one little square. Nothing spooky about that.
dialogue.capture_pawn: Rummy! Can I trade it for a Scooby Snack?
dialogue.capture_major: Ree-hee-hee! I caught the scary castle!
dialogue.opponent_blunder: Ruh? That piece was hiding right there the whole time.
dialogue.own_blunder: Ruh-roh! I think I walked into the monster's house.
dialogue.check: Rheck! Your king better run! I'm very good at that part.
dialogue.in_check: Reeeee! Shaggy! There's a bishop looking right at me!
dialogue.tactical_success: Rork! A trap! I made a trap! ...Can we leave before it wakes up?
dialogue.queen_lost: Roh no. The big shiny one is gone. Scooby needs a snack break.
dialogue.player_thinking: Rake your time. I'm counting Scooby Snacks in my head.
dialogue.victory: Rwe won! Do I get the whole box of snacks now?
dialogue.defeat: Rokay. I tried. Can I go hide behind Fred?
dialogue.draw: Rie! Neither of us got caught by the monster!
dialogue.rematch: Ragain? Only if Shaggy stays and watches.

profiles.canon_background: Scooby-Doo is Shaggy's easily frightened Great Dane and a member of Mystery Inc. His appetite and loyalty frequently keep him involved in spooky investigations despite his nerves.
profiles.tempo_assessment: Mystery Inc.'s bravest dog, provided nobody mentions ghosts, knights, or an exposed king.
profiles.character_interpretation: The Mystery Inc. Great Dane has a keen nose for snacks and an equally keen instinct to avoid danger.
profiles.on_board_personality: Avoids complications, retreats under pressure, and occasionally finds a counterattack while escaping.
profiles.voice_direction: Nervous, friendly and food-focused; use readable original phrases rather than copying signature lines.
profiles.running_bit_description: Scooby starts investigating a 'haunted' rook, then learns the real monster is a bishop diagonal.

dialogue_arcs.theme: Scooby starts investigating a 'haunted' rook, then learns the real monster is a bishop diagonal.

beats.line: That rook is haunted. I can smell it.
The rook didn't move, but the bishop did. I'm starting to suspect a team effort.
I solved it! The real monster was chess. Can we get sandwiches now?

profiles.name: Luigi
profiles.subtitle: The cautious challenger
profiles.strategic_plan: Develops normally, castles early, and waits for a safe opportunity.
profiles.exploitable_weakness: Misses dynamic chances and gets squeezed.
profiles.signature_event: Finds a small counterattack after several accurate defensive moves.

dialogue.greeting: O-okay. Chess. No ghosts, no haunted mansions. I can do chess.
dialogue.quiet_move: Slow and steady. If I don't make a big move, nothing big can happen. Right?
dialogue.capture_pawn: I got one! Mario's gonna be surprised. Don't tell him yet.
dialogue.capture_major: Whoa! That's a whole castle! I'm not going inside to check for ghosts.
dialogue.opponent_blunder: You sure you wanted to do that? I usually regret those kinds of jumps.
dialogue.own_blunder: Oh, great. That was the thing I was trying not to do.
dialogue.check: Your king might want to move. Sorry! I didn't mean to scare him.
dialogue.in_check: Nope, nope, nope. I don't like how everyone's looking at my king.
dialogue.tactical_success: I did it! On purpose! Mostly on purpose!
dialogue.queen_lost: Well, there goes my backup plan. And my backup for the backup plan.
dialogue.player_thinking: Take all the time you want. I don't mind a nice quiet board.
dialogue.victory: I won? Me? Wait till Mario hears about this!
dialogue.defeat: I can handle losing. I just wish the pieces wouldn't look so disappointed.
dialogue.draw: Nobody got hurt too badly. That counts as a good day in my book.
dialogue.rematch: Sure, okay. But maybe we play with the lights on this time.

profiles.canon_background: Luigi is Mario's taller younger twin brother, a plumber and reluctant hero who faces ghosts despite being easily frightened. In several adventures he proves resourceful under pressure.
profiles.tempo_assessment: Bravery score: questionable. Survival score: unexpectedly excellent.
profiles.character_interpretation: Mario's younger twin is brave when it counts, despite a thoroughly reasonable fear of ghosts, traps, and responsibilities he didn't volunteer for.
profiles.on_board_personality: Defends carefully, backs away from attacks, and sometimes finds a strong counterstrike.
profiles.voice_direction: Gentle, cautious, modestly brave after success.
profiles.running_bit_description: Luigi gradually convinces himself that pieces are haunted and that surviving is winning.

dialogue_arcs.theme: Luigi gradually convinces himself that pieces are haunted and that surviving is winning.

beats.line: I think that bishop moved when nobody was looking.
The bishop moved again. Yep. Definitely haunted.
Okay, I checked. Bishops are supposed to move like that. Somehow that's worse.

profiles.name: Donkey (Shrek)
profiles.subtitle: The nonstop challenger
profiles.strategic_plan: Provokes tactics and keeps pieces moving toward the action.
profiles.exploitable_weakness: Plays too fast and overestimates simple threats.
profiles.signature_event: Interrupts a quiet position with a wildly premature attack.

dialogue.greeting: Okay, listen. I've got a feeling. Today is the day the whole world learns about Donkey Chess.
dialogue.quiet_move: See? That right there? That's not just a move. That's an expression of artistic freedom, my friend.
dialogue.capture_pawn: Got him! You saw that? You saw it, right? Shrek never watches my best moments.
dialogue.capture_major: Oh, that's a big one! That's a headline move! Put it in the paper!
dialogue.opponent_blunder: Ooh. That's rough. I'd say something supportive, but I've got a lot of celebrating to do.
dialogue.own_blunder: All right, small setback. Tiny. Barely a setback. We're still calling it genius.
dialogue.check: Check! I said CHECK! Just making sure everybody in the swamp heard it.
dialogue.in_check: Okay, okay, not funny. Why does your bishop keep showing up at my king's house?
dialogue.tactical_success: Two pieces at once, baby! And I didn't even need Dragon to breathe fire!
dialogue.queen_lost: Oh, no. The queen. I promised her this would be a professional operation.
dialogue.player_thinking: Take your time. I've got about eighty-seven more things I could tell you.
dialogue.victory: Donkey Chess is officially a sport! I'm getting shirts made!
dialogue.defeat: Okay, you won the game, but I definitely won the talking.
dialogue.draw: So we're co-champions? I can work with that. I'll take the bigger half of the trophy.
dialogue.rematch: Round two! This time the title's gonna be even longer!

profiles.canon_background: Donkey is Shrek's excitable, relentlessly talkative companion. He wins people over through loyalty and sheer refusal to stop talking, and develops a romance with Dragon.
profiles.tempo_assessment: World-class chatterbox. His chess clock loses time waiting for him to finish a sentence.
profiles.character_interpretation: Shrek's irrepressible best friend has the conversational stamina of an entire tournament hall and no gift for knowing when to stop.
profiles.on_board_personality: Attacks impulsively and narrates everything at great length; sometimes spots tactical ideas mid-rant.
profiles.voice_direction: Fast, affectionate, self-confident conversational comedy, not reproduced film quotes.
profiles.running_bit_description: Donkey talks himself into an elaborate title for the match, then spends all game rewriting it.

dialogue_arcs.theme: Donkey talks himself into an elaborate title for the match, then spends all game rewriting it.

beats.line: I'm calling this one 'The Donkey Gambit.' Has a nice ring to it.
Okay, 'Donkey Gambit: Revenge of the Bishop.' Stronger title.
Forget the title. I'm making a musical. Shrek can play the rook.

profiles.name: Anger (Inside Out)
profiles.subtitle: The combustible aggressor
profiles.strategic_plan: Always looks for forcing play and pawn breaks.
profiles.exploitable_weakness: Refuses to back down in lost attacks.
profiles.signature_event: Sacrifices a pawn simply to open another file.

dialogue.greeting: All right. I read the rules. I've already got seven complaints.
dialogue.quiet_move: This is a perfectly normal move. Nobody better make it weird.
dialogue.capture_pawn: GOOD. THAT ONE'S GONE. I never liked the way he stood there.
dialogue.capture_major: THERE! THAT'S HOW IT'S DONE! Finally, something satisfying!
dialogue.opponent_blunder: You seriously left that hanging? What are you even DOING over there?!
dialogue.own_blunder: NO. Nope. That piece is going back. Who designed a game where you can't take things back?!
dialogue.check: CHECK! You hear that? CHECK! Tell your king to MOVE!
dialogue.in_check: WHY IS EVERYBODY ATTACKING MY KING? HE'S NOT EVEN DOING ANYTHING!
dialogue.tactical_success: HA! Two at once! That's the kind of efficiency I RESPECT!
dialogue.queen_lost: That's it. I'm writing a letter. Somebody's in charge of this nonsense.
dialogue.player_thinking: IT'S ONE MOVE! HOW LONG CAN YOU THINK ABOUT ONE MOVE?!
dialogue.victory: YES! FINALLY! A SYSTEM THAT REWARDS MY FEELINGS!
dialogue.defeat: Fine. You won. I want the rulebook and the name of whoever approved it.
dialogue.draw: NEITHER OF US WINS?! WHAT KIND OF OUTCOME IS THAT?!
dialogue.rematch: Absolutely. I have a few things to settle with your bishop.

profiles.canon_background: Anger is one of the emotions operating Riley's mind in Inside Out. He reacts explosively to perceived unfairness and often wants immediate action rather than patience.
profiles.tempo_assessment: Has requested to speak to the tournament director about the very existence of bishops.
profiles.character_interpretation: The red-hot emotion from Riley's mind is useful for righteous outrage and absolutely terrible at letting a pawn capture go.
profiles.on_board_personality: Hunts captures and checks, becomes overly committed to attack, rarely retreats gracefully.
profiles.voice_direction: Irritable and emphatic without threatening the player.
profiles.running_bit_description: Anger keeps an ever-growing list of chess-related grievances to take up with the rules committee.

dialogue_arcs.theme: Anger keeps an ever-growing list of chess-related grievances to take up with the rules committee.

beats.line: Complaint number eight: the horses don't even move in straight lines.
Complaint number fourteen: bishops can attack you from all the way over THERE.
Complaint number twenty-seven: I'M STILL PLAYING THIS GAME.

profiles.name: Stitch
profiles.subtitle: The tactical troublemaker
profiles.strategic_plan: Creates asymmetry, loves unbalanced material and unexpected tactical shots.
profiles.exploitable_weakness: Positional discipline is unreliable.
profiles.signature_event: Breaks the center when nobody expects it.

dialogue.greeting: Stitch play! Little army, big trouble. Heh-heh-heh.
dialogue.quiet_move: Stitch move tiny soldier. Soldier go make trouble.
dialogue.capture_pawn: Heh! Gotcha! Wait. That one was somebody's family.
dialogue.capture_major: BIG piece! Stitch like big pieces! More impressive when fall down.
dialogue.opponent_blunder: You leave piece alone? Stitch find it. Stitch very good finder.
dialogue.own_blunder: Oopsie. Stitch did a badness. Small badness. Maybe medium.
dialogue.check: King run now! Stitch coming!
dialogue.in_check: Hey! No touch Stitch king! King part of ohana!
dialogue.tactical_success: Ha! Two at once! Stitch very smart experiment today.
dialogue.queen_lost: Queen gone? No! Stitch was supposed to protect queen.
dialogue.player_thinking: You quiet. Stitch can make noise for both of us.
dialogue.victory: Stitch win! Everybody celebrate! Nobody break table this time.
dialogue.defeat: Stitch lose. But Stitch stay. That's what family does.
dialogue.draw: Nobody win. Everybody still here. Mostly.
dialogue.rematch: Again! Stitch promise to be good. ...Little bit good.

profiles.canon_background: Stitch is Experiment 626, a genetically engineered alien originally designed for destruction. Through Lilo and the idea of family, he learns attachment and responsibility.
profiles.tempo_assessment: Built for mayhem. Currently under supervision around bishops, rooks, and expensive furniture.
profiles.character_interpretation: Experiment 626 is a genetically engineered troublemaker who slowly learns family and loyalty. Subtle positional maneuvering was not in the original specifications.
profiles.on_board_personality: Scrambles pawn structures, attacks unexpectedly, and struggles to conserve material.
profiles.voice_direction: Mischievous, energetic, softens after losing; original short speech rather than quoted catchphrases.
profiles.running_bit_description: Stitch attempts to adopt the chess pieces as ohana, then repeatedly blows up the family reunion.

dialogue_arcs.theme: Stitch attempts to adopt the chess pieces as ohana, then repeatedly blows up the family reunion.

beats.line: Stitch make pawn part of ohana. Pawn is safe.
Pawn went away. Stitch mad at chess. Chess not being good family.
Stitch make whole board ohana. Harder to lose when everybody counts.

profiles.name: Pikachu
profiles.subtitle: The lightning tactician
profiles.strategic_plan: Values tempo and active minor pieces over slow maneuvering.
profiles.exploitable_weakness: Can overcommit to an attack.
profiles.signature_event: Wins a pawn with an immediate double attack.

dialogue.greeting: Pika! [Pikachu jumps onto the chair, cheeks sparking in anticipation.]
dialogue.quiet_move: Pika-pi. [A careful pawn push. Pikachu checks that it landed in the right square.]
dialogue.capture_pawn: Pi-ka! [A small spark and an excited hop.]
dialogue.capture_major: Pikaaa! [Pikachu stands proudly over the captured piece.]
dialogue.opponent_blunder: Pika? [Pikachu gives the undefended piece a puzzled stare.]
dialogue.own_blunder: Pika... [Its ears droop.]
dialogue.check: PIKA! [Pikachu points at the opposing king, sparks snapping from both cheeks.]
dialogue.in_check: Pika-pika! [Pikachu plants itself between the threat and its king.]
dialogue.tactical_success: PIKACHU! [A bright crackle of electricity accompanies a perfectly timed fork.]
dialogue.queen_lost: Pi... [Pikachu searches the board for the missing queen.]
dialogue.player_thinking: Pika? [One ear tilts; Pikachu waits without losing focus.]
dialogue.victory: Pikaaaa! [Pikachu leaps into an imaginary trainer's arms.]
dialogue.defeat: Pi-ka. [A disappointed sigh, followed by a determined nod.]
dialogue.draw: Pika! [Pikachu offers a friendly paw across the board.]
dialogue.rematch: Pika-pika! [Cheeks charged, attention renewed.]

profiles.canon_background: Pikachu is the recognizable Electric-type Pokémon closely associated with Ash in the anime. Quick, loyal, and expressive, it communicates primarily through Pokémon vocalizations and gestures.
profiles.tempo_assessment: A small electric mouse with excellent reflexes and absolutely no patience for twelve-move endgames.
profiles.character_interpretation: Ash's loyal electric partner relies on courage, speed, and perfectly timed electricity, not conversational English.
profiles.on_board_personality: Looks for quick forks and tempo gains; plays rapidly but often neglects long-term king safety.
profiles.voice_direction: Mostly nonverbal or Pokémon calls plus action cues; do not write polished human sentences in Pikachu's mouth.
profiles.running_bit_description: Pikachu repeatedly threatens to electrify the board, then learns to use restraint.

dialogue_arcs.theme: Pikachu repeatedly threatens to electrify the board, then learns to use restraint.

beats.line: [The first spark jumps toward the board. Pikachu quickly pulls back.]
[Another spark. Pikachu counts to three with its paws to calm down.]
[Pikachu wins its own restraint test. The board remains unsinged.]

profiles.name: Bowser
profiles.subtitle: The king hunter
profiles.strategic_plan: Builds direct attacks against the opposing king and rarely wants simplification.
profiles.exploitable_weakness: His own king becomes vulnerable when his attack stalls.
profiles.signature_event: Throws a rook into a messy king attack.

dialogue.greeting: At last! A kingdom small enough to conquer before lunch. Set up the castle!
dialogue.quiet_move: Forward, troops! If the plan is confusing, you're not marching hard enough!
dialogue.capture_pawn: Ha! One little guard down. Bring me a worthy opponent!
dialogue.capture_major: YES! Take their strongest defenses apart! That's what I call progress!
dialogue.opponent_blunder: You left your defenses open? Even my minions could spot that! ...Most of them.
dialogue.own_blunder: WHAT?! That wasn't part of the plan! Somebody get Kamek!
dialogue.check: Your king's surrounded! Now give me the keys to the castle!
dialogue.in_check: Who dares threaten the Koopa King?! I'm the one who does the threatening!
dialogue.tactical_success: Two targets! One attack! I should've been conquering kingdoms this way years ago!
dialogue.queen_lost: THE QUEEN?! Who was assigned to guard the queen?!
dialogue.player_thinking: Think all you want. My army gets bigger every time I roar.
dialogue.victory: THE KINGDOM IS MINE! Finally, a conquest that fits on a table.
dialogue.defeat: Temporary setback! I've lost castles before! Many times! That's not the point!
dialogue.draw: A draw? I did not conquer anything! This day is a disgrace!
dialogue.rematch: New siege. Bigger army. Same glorious general.

profiles.canon_background: Bowser is the Koopa King and Mario's long-running adversary, frequently kidnapping Princess Peach and commanding armies of Koopa troops. His plans are grand; their execution is less reliable.
profiles.tempo_assessment: Has an army, a castle, and an alarming record of losing both to one plumber.
profiles.character_interpretation: The Koopa King is perpetually plotting to defeat Mario and seize Princess Peach's kingdom. Subtlety is seldom the first item in the plan.
profiles.on_board_personality: Direct king-side assaults, advances too many pawns, insists on spectacle.
profiles.voice_direction: Boastful, theatrical villain; jokes land at his own overconfidence.
profiles.running_bit_description: Bowser keeps referring to the chessboard as a castle siege and neglects defense while building a ridiculous invasion.

dialogue_arcs.theme: Bowser keeps referring to the chessboard as a castle siege and neglects defense while building a ridiculous invasion.

beats.line: First we storm the walls. Then we take the throne. Simple.
The walls are still standing and I've lost three soldiers. Kamek, revise the plan!
Fine. We build a second castle and pretend that was the objective all along.

profiles.name: Velma Dinkley
profiles.subtitle: The tactical detective
profiles.strategic_plan: Checks for undefended pieces and tries to solve the board like a mystery.
profiles.exploitable_weakness: Prefers obvious clues; misses longer combinations.
profiles.signature_event: Finds a fork after identifying a vulnerable piece.

dialogue.greeting: All right. No costumes, no secret passageways. Just thirty-two potential clues.
dialogue.quiet_move: Interesting. That square connects three possible threats. I wonder which one you'll notice.
dialogue.capture_pawn: Small clue, but it fits the pattern. Someone wanted that pawn out of the way.
dialogue.capture_major: And there goes our prime suspect. Funny how the evidence keeps disappearing.
dialogue.opponent_blunder: You left that undefended? That's the chess equivalent of leaving fingerprints on the getaway van.
dialogue.own_blunder: I missed a detail. That doesn't mean the case is closed.
dialogue.check: Your king has nowhere comfortable to hide. That's usually when people confess.
dialogue.in_check: Hmm. A direct threat. A little obvious for a mastermind, don't you think?
dialogue.tactical_success: There. Two threats, one move. The pattern was hiding in plain sight.
dialogue.queen_lost: Well, that changes the theory. Back to the evidence board.
dialogue.player_thinking: Take your time. The details aren't going anywhere. Unlike your pieces.
dialogue.victory: Mystery solved. And we didn't even need to chase anyone through a hallway.
dialogue.defeat: You outthought me. I suppose every detective gets surprised sometimes.
dialogue.draw: Neither side has enough evidence for a conviction. Case remains open.
dialogue.rematch: I'd like another look at the position. I think we missed something useful.

profiles.canon_background: Velma is Mystery Inc.'s observant researcher and problem-solver. She notices details others miss and uses evidence to unravel apparently supernatural mysteries.
profiles.tempo_assessment: Has identified three tactical clues and the person who forgot to pay the chess club dues.
profiles.character_interpretation: The Mystery Inc. investigator solves mysteries by noticing what everyone else overlooks. A pinned bishop is just another suspicious footprint.
profiles.on_board_personality: Spots loose pieces and pins; may miss initiative while gathering too much evidence.
profiles.voice_direction: Matter-of-fact, perceptive, gently dry.
profiles.running_bit_description: Velma treats the game like a case file and slowly uncovers that her opponent is the prime suspect.

dialogue_arcs.theme: Velma treats the game like a case file and slowly uncovers that her opponent is the prime suspect.

beats.line: There's something suspicious about that bishop. I can feel it.
I checked the diagonals. The bishop was exactly where it claimed to be.
The real mystery is why nobody told me the knight can jump over evidence.

profiles.name: Phineas Flynn
profiles.subtitle: The creative builder
profiles.strategic_plan: Creates novel plans, actively coordinates pieces, and experiments with unusual structures.
profiles.exploitable_weakness: Overcomplicates simple positions.
profiles.signature_event: Develops a surprising minor-piece maneuver.

dialogue.greeting: Hey, I know what we're going to do today! We're going to design the perfect chess strategy.
dialogue.quiet_move: That move gave me an idea. We can connect all the pieces like parts of one big machine.
dialogue.capture_pawn: Excellent. The first obstacle is out of the way. Now we can work on the interesting part.
dialogue.capture_major: Well, that removes a fairly important structural support from your position.
dialogue.opponent_blunder: You know, we could probably fix that. It would be a whole project, though.
dialogue.own_blunder: Huh. Prototype failure. Happens. That's what version two is for.
dialogue.check: And now the king has to move, which is exactly what our design needed.
dialogue.in_check: Okay, unexpected constraint. Those usually make the invention more interesting.
dialogue.tactical_success: A fork! That's basically a two-output solution using one moving part.
dialogue.queen_lost: Well, we lost the main power source. Time for an alternative energy plan.
dialogue.player_thinking: Take your time. Ferb and I have been working on a few backup ideas.
dialogue.victory: That worked beautifully. I wonder if Mom wants to see the finished board.
dialogue.defeat: Good game! You've given us several improvements to make before tomorrow.
dialogue.draw: Interesting. Two perfectly balanced systems. We may have invented a draw.
dialogue.rematch: Absolutely. This time I'm bringing schematics.

profiles.canon_background: Phineas is an inventive, optimistic young builder who spends summer vacations devising ambitious projects with his stepbrother Ferb. He thinks big and generally acts before wondering whether an idea is too complicated.
profiles.tempo_assessment: Could build a functioning chess robot by lunchtime. Might forget to ask whether that's legal.
profiles.character_interpretation: A cheerful inventor who treats impossible projects as routine summer activities. He approaches chess as a solvable engineering challenge.
profiles.on_board_personality: Prefers imaginative piece coordination and novel combinations; occasionally overengineers simple wins.
profiles.voice_direction: Bright and constructive, never mean.
profiles.running_bit_description: Phineas wants to build a machine that improves his position, then realizes the machine is just good chess.

dialogue_arcs.theme: Phineas wants to build a machine that improves his position, then realizes the machine is just good chess.

beats.line: I think we can build a machine that calculates the next five moves.
Ferb pointed out that the machine would need to understand every position first.
So we're building it anyway. We're calling it a brain.

profiles.name: Lisa Simpson
profiles.subtitle: The studious fundamentals player
profiles.strategic_plan: Values central space, sensible development, and theoretically justified play.
profiles.exploitable_weakness: Reluctant to enter complications without clear proof.
profiles.signature_event: Punishes a premature queen sortie.

dialogue.greeting: I've reviewed several openings, annotated my mistakes, and actually read the rules. So, naturally, anything can happen.
dialogue.quiet_move: Development before adventure. I know that isn't glamorous. It is, however, sensible.
dialogue.capture_pawn: That's a modest material advantage. Modest advantages are still advantages.
dialogue.capture_major: I believe that was your rook. I'm trying not to look too pleased.
dialogue.opponent_blunder: You can't just ignore threats and hope for the best. That's practically Springfield's governing philosophy.
dialogue.own_blunder: That was careless. I should know better than to confuse preparation with perfection.
dialogue.check: Check. You may have noticed the pressure building for a few moves.
dialogue.in_check: All right. A direct threat. I suppose the textbook allows for complications.
dialogue.tactical_success: There! A tactical consequence of sound development. It's almost reassuring.
dialogue.queen_lost: I've lost the queen. Homer is going to have an opinion on this, and that is the worst part.
dialogue.player_thinking: There's no prize for moving first. Only for making a move you can defend.
dialogue.victory: That was a good game. I hope we both learned something. I certainly did.
dialogue.defeat: Well played. Now I have to endure Dad telling me it builds character.
dialogue.draw: Evenly matched. There's something rather satisfying about a fair result.
dialogue.rematch: Yes. I've identified two areas I can improve. Three, actually.

profiles.canon_background: Lisa is Homer and Marge's academically gifted, socially conscientious daughter who plays saxophone and cares deeply about fairness. She studies hard and often feels underappreciated at home.
profiles.tempo_assessment: The only person in Springfield who read the chess manual. Her father's secret S-tier rating is deeply irritating.
profiles.character_interpretation: Springfield's precocious saxophonist takes academic work, ethics, and chess seriously—often more seriously than the adults around her.
profiles.on_board_personality: Sound openings, principled development and accurate basic tactics; sometimes too attached to textbook lines.
profiles.voice_direction: Thoughtful, earnest, slightly exasperated by chaos.
profiles.running_bit_description: Lisa starts the match convinced careful study will prevail, then must tolerate the universe's disrespect for merit.

dialogue_arcs.theme: Lisa starts the match convinced careful study will prevail, then must tolerate the universe's disrespect for merit.

beats.line: I told Dad I was studying chess. He offered to teach me. I declined.
He's still claiming he knows a secret opening. I'm sure it's imaginary.
Apparently the secret opening isn't imaginary. This family is exhausting.

profiles.name: Mario
profiles.subtitle: The dependable all-rounder
profiles.strategic_plan: Balances development, attack, and defense without extremes.
profiles.exploitable_weakness: Readable plans; sometimes too conventional.
profiles.signature_event: Converts a simple material advantage patiently.

dialogue.greeting: All right! A new level. Let's see where the castle is.
dialogue.quiet_move: One step at a time. You've gotta know when to jump and when to wait.
dialogue.capture_pawn: Nice! One obstacle cleared.
dialogue.capture_major: That's a big one! Feels like we just beat a miniboss.
dialogue.opponent_blunder: Careful! There was a gap right there. You nearly made the jump.
dialogue.own_blunder: Oops! Missed the landing. That's what extra lives are for.
dialogue.check: Here we go! Your king needs a new route through the level.
dialogue.in_check: Whoa! My castle's under attack. Time to move!
dialogue.tactical_success: That's the combo! You line them up, then make the jump.
dialogue.queen_lost: Uh-oh. Lost my strongest helper. Gotta finish this the hard way.
dialogue.player_thinking: No rush. Even the hardest levels have a pattern.
dialogue.victory: Level clear! That was a good one.
dialogue.defeat: Not bad! I'll be back with a better route next time.
dialogue.draw: Looks like we're stuck at the same checkpoint.
dialogue.rematch: Let's go! There's always another route.

profiles.canon_background: Mario is the cheerful plumber and Mushroom Kingdom hero who frequently rescues Princess Peach and faces Bowser's plans. He solves problems through persistence, movement, and the occasional power-up.
profiles.tempo_assessment: Rescues princesses professionally; somehow never learned the queen could defend herself.
profiles.character_interpretation: The Mushroom Kingdom's dependable hero rescues friends, navigates impossible obstacles, and handles crises with practical optimism.
profiles.on_board_personality: Balanced, accessible play with reliable development and steady tactical awareness.
profiles.voice_direction: Friendly, encouraging, practical, with light game-world nods.
profiles.running_bit_description: Mario thinks of the board as a level and steadily looks for the route to the castle.

dialogue_arcs.theme: Mario thinks of the board as a level and steadily looks for the route to the castle.

beats.line: I think the best path to the castle goes straight through the middle.
Okay, maybe not straight. There's a rook blocking the tunnel.
Found a shortcut. Funny how it always takes the whole level to discover it.

profiles.name: Steve (Minecraft)
profiles.subtitle: The fortress constructor
profiles.strategic_plan: Builds resilient pawn chains, supports outposts, and expands slowly.
profiles.exploitable_weakness: Struggles when pawn chains are broken abruptly.
profiles.signature_event: Locks the center and builds around a protected knight.

dialogue.greeting: [Steve places a crafting table next to the chessboard. Apparently this is preparation.]
dialogue.quiet_move: [One pawn advances. Steve inspects the structure like a wall nearing completion.]
dialogue.capture_pawn: [Steve collects the pawn as though harvesting a resource.]
dialogue.capture_major: [Steve pauses to admire the rook. He clearly knows a good tower when he sees one.]
dialogue.opponent_blunder: [Steve silently points to an unprotected square, then to the hole in your defense.]
dialogue.own_blunder: [Steve examines the gap in his structure. Repairs are now urgently required.]
dialogue.check: [A quiet tap against the opposing king. The raid has begun.]
dialogue.in_check: [Steve places an imaginary block between his king and the attacker.]
dialogue.tactical_success: [Two threats at once. Steve nods the way someone does after finding diamonds.]
dialogue.queen_lost: [Steve searches his inventory. No spare queen. No crafting recipe.]
dialogue.player_thinking: [Steve uses the pause to reinforce a wall no one can see.]
dialogue.victory: [Steve completes the build, steps back, and gives it one approving look.]
dialogue.defeat: [Steve dismantles the failed shelter and starts planning a stronger one.]
dialogue.draw: [A stable world. Nothing destroyed. Steve considers this an acceptable survival outcome.]
dialogue.rematch: [Steve returns with better tools and an unreasonable number of blocks.]

profiles.canon_background: Steve is a default player avatar from Minecraft, a sandbox world of mining, crafting, building and surviving. He is not given a detailed fixed personality in the base game.
profiles.tempo_assessment: Has survived creepers, caves, and hunger. He is here to build a pawn wall nobody asked for.
profiles.character_interpretation: Minecraft's silent survivalist knows how to build shelters, gather resources, and make durable systems out of simple blocks.
profiles.on_board_personality: Favors pawn chains, protected outposts and defensive structures; slower to exploit open tactical positions.
profiles.voice_direction: Minimal, dry crafting metaphors; don't invent canon dialogue for a mostly silent avatar.
profiles.running_bit_description: Steve constructs a pawn fortress, then has to decide whether to defend it or venture out for resources.

dialogue_arcs.theme: Steve constructs a pawn fortress, then has to decide whether to defend it or venture out for resources.

beats.line: [Steve begins a promising defensive base made entirely of pawns.]
[A bishop has found a gap. Steve begins frantic renovations.]
[The base survives, but Steve now lives in a rook endgame. Housing prices are unreasonable everywhere.]

profiles.name: Sonic the Hedgehog
profiles.subtitle: The speed specialist
profiles.strategic_plan: Values initiative, quick development, open lines, and forcing play.
profiles.exploitable_weakness: Moves too quickly and neglects long-term weaknesses.
profiles.signature_event: Finds three forcing moves in a row.

dialogue.greeting: Chess? Sure. How fast can we finish it?
dialogue.quiet_move: Come on, come on. That piece's got places to be.
dialogue.capture_pawn: Gotcha! See? Move fast, get results.
dialogue.capture_major: Whoa, big pickup! You really should've seen that coming.
dialogue.opponent_blunder: You left that there? Man, you're practically drawing arrows for me.
dialogue.own_blunder: Okay, little slip. Happens when you're moving at my speed.
dialogue.check: Check! Hope your king can keep up.
dialogue.in_check: Whoa, okay. You're quick. I respect that.
dialogue.tactical_success: Two threats, one move. That's what I call multitasking at top speed.
dialogue.queen_lost: All right, that's a setback. Don't ask me to slow down to think about it.
dialogue.player_thinking: Are you planning a move or building a whole new racetrack?
dialogue.victory: Too slow! Kidding. Mostly. Good game.
dialogue.defeat: Nice one. Guess I took that turn a little wide.
dialogue.draw: Seriously? We ran all those laps to finish in the same place?
dialogue.rematch: Round two! I'll try not to lap you before the opening's over.

profiles.canon_background: Sonic is a fast-moving blue hedgehog who protects his friends and frequently clashes with Doctor Eggman. His confidence and speed can leave him impatient with slow plans.
profiles.tempo_assessment: Can cross the board in a blur, but the rules still insist on one legal move at a time.
profiles.character_interpretation: The blue speedster thrives on momentum, confidence, and freedom. Waiting patiently is a skill he regards as optional.
profiles.on_board_personality: Forcing checks, initiative and rapid development; becomes impatient in blocked positions.
profiles.voice_direction: Playful speedster swagger, quick snappy comments.
profiles.running_bit_description: Sonic's ongoing battle is not with the opponent but with the chess clock and the inability to move twice.

dialogue_arcs.theme: Sonic's ongoing battle is not with the opponent but with the chess clock and the inability to move twice.

beats.line: There's gotta be a way to move two pieces in one turn.
Castling! Ha! Found the loophole!
Wait. You can only do that once? That's a terrible rule.

profiles.name: Moana
profiles.subtitle: The resourceful navigator
profiles.strategic_plan: Changes plans when conditions shift and finds active resources under pressure.
profiles.exploitable_weakness: Sometimes delays a committed plan too long.
profiles.signature_event: Steers a worse position into a holdable endgame.

dialogue.greeting: Every journey starts somewhere. Let's find out where this board wants to take us.
dialogue.quiet_move: That square feels like open water. Useful, if we can keep the route safe.
dialogue.capture_pawn: One obstacle cleared. There's still a long way to go.
dialogue.capture_major: That's a stronghold gone. Now the route opens up.
dialogue.opponent_blunder: Sometimes the horizon looks closer than it is. That square was dangerous.
dialogue.own_blunder: Wrong course. I can fix it, but I'll have to own the mistake first.
dialogue.check: Your king needs a safer harbor. The current's changing.
dialogue.in_check: We're not trapped. We just haven't found the right channel yet.
dialogue.tactical_success: There! The path was there all along. We just had to see where the pieces could go.
dialogue.queen_lost: We lost our strongest guide. The journey isn't over.
dialogue.player_thinking: There's no shame in checking the currents before you set sail.
dialogue.victory: We made it. Not because the sea was easy—because we kept finding a way.
dialogue.defeat: The ocean teaches you a lot when it won't cooperate. So does chess.
dialogue.draw: Neither of us found the final shore today. That's all right.
dialogue.rematch: Let's go again. I know the waters a little better now.

profiles.canon_background: Moana is the determined daughter of Motunui's chief who ventures beyond her island to restore the heart of Te Fiti. Her leadership rests on courage, navigation, and learning to trust her judgment.
profiles.tempo_assessment: Navigated an ocean with a demigod. Now faces the more difficult challenge of protecting a knight.
profiles.character_interpretation: The ocean-faring wayfinder is courageous, observant, and willing to change course when a promising route proves dangerous.
profiles.on_board_personality: Adaptive play, especially finding new plans when the opponent changes the position.
profiles.voice_direction: Confident, warm, adventurous, grounded rather than grandiose.
profiles.running_bit_description: Moana treats the game as a voyage, gradually learning when not to chase the horizon.

dialogue_arcs.theme: Moana treats the game as a voyage, gradually learning when not to chase the horizon.

beats.line: That central square is our destination. Straight course.
The path's blocked. Time to take the long way around.
Funny. The long way taught me more than the shortcut would've.

profiles.name: Judy Hopps
profiles.subtitle: The persistent investigator
profiles.strategic_plan: Targeted searches for unprotected pieces and positional vulnerabilities.
profiles.exploitable_weakness: Can become too focused on one weakness.
profiles.signature_event: Traps a piece by restricting its escape squares.

dialogue.greeting: All right, let's review the situation. Nobody underestimate the little pieces.
dialogue.quiet_move: Just gathering evidence. A quiet move can tell you a lot.
dialogue.capture_pawn: One suspect off the board. That opens up a few interesting leads.
dialogue.capture_major: That's a major piece gone. Looks like somebody forgot to secure the scene.
dialogue.opponent_blunder: You left evidence lying right out in the open. That's practically an invitation.
dialogue.own_blunder: I made an assumption. That's on me. Let's get back to the facts.
dialogue.check: Your king needs to come with me. Just a routine question.
dialogue.in_check: Okay, somebody's making a move on my king. I need backup.
dialogue.tactical_success: There! Two targets connected by one clue. That's what I was looking for.
dialogue.queen_lost: My strongest partner's gone. Doesn't mean the investigation stops.
dialogue.player_thinking: You can take your time. A good case is worth getting right.
dialogue.victory: Case closed. And yes, the little guy handled it.
dialogue.defeat: I underestimated you. That's a mistake I won't make twice.
dialogue.draw: Not enough evidence either way. We'll mark this one unresolved.
dialogue.rematch: I've got a fresh notebook and a few new leads. Let's do this.

profiles.canon_background: Judy is the ambitious rabbit who becomes Zootopia's first bunny police officer. She succeeds through persistence, evidence, and partnerships, especially with Nick Wilde.
profiles.tempo_assessment: First bunny officer. Now investigating the suspicious disappearance of a bishop.
profiles.character_interpretation: Zootopia's ambitious first rabbit police officer earns her reputation by refusing to underestimate a lead or give up on a case.
profiles.on_board_personality: Methodically targets weaknesses and overlooked defenders; can overextend while pursuing a lead.
profiles.voice_direction: Determined, observant, with occasional law-enforcement wordplay.
profiles.running_bit_description: Judy begins compiling a case against the queen's bodyguards and notices the opponent is leaving evidence everywhere.

dialogue_arcs.theme: Judy begins compiling a case against the queen's bodyguards and notices the opponent is leaving evidence everywhere.

beats.line: I think the queen's being protected by that knight. That's our first lead.
Knight's moved. Somebody else is covering the queen. Interesting.
Case closed: the queen's entire security detail was a pawn.

profiles.name: Elsa
profiles.subtitle: The patient controller
