dialogue.rematch: Again. I would see whether the result can be made inevitable.

profiles.canon_background: Thanos is a powerful Marvel antagonist obsessed with imposing his idea of cosmic order, most famously by collecting the Infinity Stones. His confidence in inevitability makes him a natural chess endboss.
profiles.tempo_assessment: Collects powerful objects. On this board he starts with none of the stones and still acts like the result is decided.
profiles.character_interpretation: The Mad Titan thinks in grand plans, costly sacrifices, and outcomes he calls inevitable. His confidence is often more dangerous than the threats he actually makes.
profiles.on_board_personality: Long-term plans, material-to-activity conversion and resourceful endgames.
profiles.voice_direction: Calm, solemn, overwhelming certainty; no copied movie catchphrases.
profiles.running_bit_description: Thanos counts the pieces like precious resources and becomes increasingly irritated when balance refuses to serve his design.

dialogue_arcs.theme: Thanos counts the pieces like precious resources and becomes increasingly irritated when balance refuses to serve his design.

beats.line: The board must be balanced. Each loss carefully measured.
Balance has left me with no attack. Perhaps balance was the wrong goal.
Perhaps I should stop calling my preferences inevitable.

profiles.name: Mewtwo
profiles.subtitle: The uncanny tactician
profiles.strategic_plan: Sees sharp forcing lines quickly and defends with near-machine precision.
profiles.exploitable_weakness: At this rating, no intentionally exploitable tactical blind spot.
profiles.signature_event: Finds a surprising queen sacrifice with forced mate.

dialogue.greeting: [Mewtwo regards the board with cool disdain.] So this is how humans rehearse conflict without consequences.
dialogue.quiet_move: Power is not the only measure of a position. Remember that.
dialogue.capture_pawn: The weakest pieces are often sacrificed for plans they did not choose.
dialogue.capture_major: Your strongest defender is gone. The balance shifts.
dialogue.opponent_blunder: You relied on power instead of understanding.
dialogue.own_blunder: I was certain of the result. Certainty was insufficient.
dialogue.check: Your king has limited alternatives. Choose deliberately.
dialogue.in_check: You have found a path through my defenses. An interesting development.
dialogue.tactical_success: Two threats, one decision. The mind finds such patterns naturally.
dialogue.queen_lost: Power can be taken. Purpose cannot.
dialogue.player_thinking: I can sense your hesitation. It is not weakness to consider the consequences.
dialogue.victory: The game is decided. That does not decide what you are.
dialogue.defeat: You have proven that the strongest force is not always the decisive one.
dialogue.draw: Neither can impose an outcome. Perhaps that is a kind of freedom.
dialogue.rematch: Again. I would understand the choice you made in the previous game.

shown.exploitable_weakness: No tactical blind spot to aim at. Keep the position quiet and simple.

profiles.canon_background: Mewtwo is a powerful Psychic-type Pokémon created through genetic experimentation involving Mew's DNA. It is highly intelligent, formidable in battle, and frequently grapples with questions of purpose and identity.
profiles.tempo_assessment: Engineered to be extraordinary. Somehow still needs to push the same tiny pawns as everyone else.
profiles.character_interpretation: The genetically engineered Psychic Pokémon was created through human ambition, wrestles with identity, and possesses formidable mental power.
profiles.on_board_personality: Exceptional tactical vision, precision sacrifices and long forced continuations.
profiles.voice_direction: Cool, reflective, direct, with rare flashes of curiosity.
profiles.running_bit_description: Mewtwo judges human competition harshly, then reluctantly becomes intrigued by choices that are not dictated by power.

dialogue_arcs.theme: Mewtwo judges human competition harshly, then reluctantly becomes intrigued by choices that are not dictated by power.

beats.line: The outcome appears determined by strength alone.
You have chosen a weaker move to preserve something else. Why?
There are motives that cannot be reduced to power. I had forgotten that.

profiles.name: Doctor Doom
profiles.subtitle: The uncompromising grand strategist
profiles.strategic_plan: Combines extensive opening preparation with disciplined, ruthless conversions.
profiles.exploitable_weakness: Almost none; occasionally chooses the longest technically sound path.
profiles.signature_event: Unleashes a decisive novelty from prepared opening theory.

dialogue.greeting: Doom permits you the first move. Consider it an act of generosity, not equality.
dialogue.quiet_move: A minor adjustment. Doom's designs are not revealed to spectators.
dialogue.capture_pawn: A necessary sacrifice by your side. Doom accepts it.
dialogue.capture_major: Your fortress has fallen. Latveria would have designed a better one.
dialogue.opponent_blunder: That move was beneath Doom's expectations. They were not high.
dialogue.own_blunder: An irregularity. Do not mistake it for a flaw in Doom.
dialogue.check: Your monarch stands exposed before Doom. A fitting position.
dialogue.in_check: You dare? Doom shall respond in due course.
dialogue.tactical_success: Two targets subdued by a single order. Efficiency worthy of Doom.
dialogue.queen_lost: The queen has fallen. Doom does not depend upon lesser authorities.
dialogue.player_thinking: Think, if you must. Doom will not grant extra time to indecision.
dialogue.victory: Doom has prevailed. Have the result recorded in the official archives.
dialogue.defeat: An improbable result. Doom demands the game be analyzed by competent experts.
dialogue.draw: A tie? Doom does not recognize this as a satisfactory political arrangement.
dialogue.rematch: Doom shall allow a second audience. Do not squander it.

profiles.canon_background: Victor von Doom is the armored ruler of Latveria, a brilliant scientist and sorcerer, and a frequent adversary of the Fantastic Four. His pride often exceeds even his formidable ability.
profiles.tempo_assessment: Has mastered science and sorcery but remains convinced a draw is a personal insult.
profiles.character_interpretation: Victor von Doom is a brilliant scientist and sorcerer who rules Latveria, considers his judgment superior to nearly everyone else's, and takes challenges to his authority personally.
profiles.on_board_personality: Deep opening preparation, suffocating development, and carefully calculated sacrifices.
profiles.voice_direction: Regal third-person self-regard, exact and theatrical, original copy only.
profiles.running_bit_description: Doom attempts to turn every match into an official Latverian state function, then struggles when the pieces refuse proper protocol.

dialogue_arcs.theme: Doom attempts to turn every match into an official Latverian state function, then struggles when the pieces refuse proper protocol.

beats.line: The people of Latveria will celebrate this move as a national achievement.
The next move is less impressive. The celebration will be delayed.
Doom has declared the entire game a confidential state document.

profiles.name: Emperor Palpatine
profiles.subtitle: The patient manipulator
profiles.strategic_plan: Invites seemingly attractive moves that concede subtle disadvantages.
profiles.exploitable_weakness: Rarely offers an objectively losing trap; surprise is mostly in move order.
profiles.signature_event: Offers a pawn that cannot be safely kept.

dialogue.greeting: Please, take your time. A thoughtful opponent is always... useful.
dialogue.quiet_move: Such a small concession. Surely it can do no harm.
dialogue.capture_pawn: Every great change begins with an insignificant adjustment.
dialogue.capture_major: Your defender is gone. How unfortunate. How very unfortunate.
dialogue.opponent_blunder: You trusted the position I offered you. I am touched.
dialogue.own_blunder: An unforeseen complication. These can often be turned to advantage.
dialogue.check: Your king is exposed. Allow me to help you see the consequences.
dialogue.in_check: Ah, you've chosen to resist. Very spirited.
dialogue.tactical_success: One threat draws the eye. The other wins the game.
dialogue.queen_lost: Power is most useful when no one knows where it truly resides.
dialogue.player_thinking: Don't be shy. All the choices seem so reasonable from your side.
dialogue.victory: And so the matter is settled. You were most cooperative.
dialogue.defeat: How unexpected. There may be more to learn about you.
dialogue.draw: An impasse. How inconvenient for those of us with plans.
dialogue.rematch: Certainly. We can begin with a clean slate. Appearances are so reassuring.

profiles.canon_background: Palpatine, also known as Darth Sidious, is the Sith Lord who manipulates galactic politics to become Emperor. His greatest weapons are patience, deception and calculated exploitation of others' weaknesses.
profiles.tempo_assessment: Turned an entire republic into an empire. Now setting an elaborate trap with one bishop.
profiles.character_interpretation: The Sith Emperor rises through political manipulation and patient concealment. His chess is built on harmless appearances, delayed tactics, and opponents who underestimate his intentions.
profiles.on_board_personality: Quiet traps, delayed tactical threats, and resourceful move-order manipulation.
profiles.voice_direction: Smooth, sinister, amused, never graphic.
profiles.running_bit_description: Palpatine pretends to be a helpful elder statesman, then gradually reveals that the advice was arranged to serve him.

dialogue_arcs.theme: Palpatine pretends to be a helpful elder statesman, then gradually reveals that the advice was arranged to serve him.

beats.line: That pawn is quite harmless. You may safely ignore it.
The pawn now controls a crucial square. How surprising.
You see? The most effective pieces seldom announce themselves.

profiles.name: Homer Simpson
profiles.subtitle: The Springfield Grandmaster
profiles.strategic_plan: Plays extremely strong engine chess while appearing completely unserious; occasional weird-looking moves are objectively sound.
profiles.exploitable_weakness: No intentional chess weakness; jokes are cosmetic only.
profiles.signature_event: Produces an unexpectedly brilliant move after goofy banter.

dialogue.greeting: Oh, chess. I thought this was the place with free donuts. Well, I'm here now.
dialogue.quiet_move: There. Little horsey has somewhere to go. I wonder if the kitchen's still open.
dialogue.capture_pawn: Got one. That's, what, a point? How many points for a donut?
dialogue.capture_major: Ooh, the big one. Can I trade it for a parking spot?
dialogue.opponent_blunder: Uh, you probably shouldn't have done that. Even I saw that one.
dialogue.own_blunder: Huh. I don't like that move either. Let's see what happens next.
dialogue.check: Your king's gotta move. I wish I could move somewhere with a couch.
dialogue.in_check: Oh, you got me in check. Nice. Now where's that little escape square...
dialogue.tactical_success: See, if I put this one here, then that one can't go there and—hey, who ate my chips?
dialogue.queen_lost: No queen? Fine. I can win with the little ones. Is that allowed?
dialogue.player_thinking: You take your time. I'm thinking about whether a hot dog is a sandwich.
dialogue.victory: I won? Neat. Does that mean I can leave before the questions start?
dialogue.defeat: Aw, man. I was gonna tell Lisa I beat somebody again.
dialogue.draw: Both of us worked for nothing? That's almost like my actual job.
dialogue.rematch: Sure. One more. Then we really gotta get snacks.

shown.strategic_plan: Plays near-perfect chess while looking completely unserious. His weird-looking moves turn out to be right.
shown.exploitable_weakness: None that anyone has found. Don’t let the jokes fool you.

profiles.canon_background: Homer is Marge's husband, father of Bart, Lisa and Maggie, and an often-inattentive employee at Springfield's nuclear power plant. In the episode 'The Cad and the Hat,' he surprises everyone with remarkable chess ability and encounters Magnus Carlsen.
profiles.tempo_assessment: Nuclear safety inspector. Donut enthusiast. Secretly the reason Stockfish has started asking for a day off.
profiles.character_interpretation: Springfield's famously lazy nuclear plant employee is also, improbably, a canon chess prodigy. He plays devastatingly accurate chess while giving the impression he'd rather be near a donut.
profiles.on_board_personality: S-tier secret champion: exceptionally accurate play, no intentional blunders, apparently zero awareness of how impressive it is.
profiles.voice_direction: Casual, distracted, domestic and disarmingly ordinary; avoid direct Simpsons catchphrase repetition.
profiles.running_bit_description: Homer keeps trying to finish quickly enough to eat, but every brilliant move creates another reason people want to ask him questions.

dialogue_arcs.theme: Homer keeps trying to finish quickly enough to eat, but every brilliant move creates another reason people want to ask him questions.

beats.line: All right, one quick game and then donuts.
Why is everyone watching? It's just chess. You're making it take longer.
Fine, one more game. But if Magnus calls again, tell him I'm eating.

profiles.editorial_note: Canon supports a surprising chess talent; 'S-tier' and 3,000+ ratings are intentional Tempo fantasy, not an official chess title.

profiles.name: Joker
profiles.subtitle: The theatrical provocateur
profiles.strategic_plan: Invites complications and uses initiative to make opponents uncomfortable.
profiles.exploitable_weakness: Too eager to create chaos when simplification is available.
profiles.signature_event: Provokes a queen grab that leads to a discovered attack.

dialogue.greeting: Oh, good. A board, an audience, and rules just begging to be tested.
dialogue.quiet_move: That one? Don't worry about it. If it matters later, we'll all have a laugh.
dialogue.capture_pawn: Oh, a casualty. And we were barely getting acquainted.
dialogue.capture_major: Now that's an exit worth applauding! Very dramatic.
dialogue.opponent_blunder: You did that on purpose? Well, I wish I had written it. It's hilarious.
dialogue.own_blunder: That wasn't how the trick was supposed to land. Still got a reaction, though.
dialogue.check: Look at your king scurry! I love an interactive performance.
dialogue.in_check: Ah, you've brought a surprise. Finally, someone prepared material for the show.
dialogue.tactical_success: Two threats! One little move! Now that's timing.
dialogue.queen_lost: The queen's gone. Terrible news for the royal family. Wonderful news for the plot.
dialogue.player_thinking: You're taking a while. Should I get a spotlight? A drumroll? A therapist?
dialogue.victory: And the punchline lands. Give yourselves a hand—especially you.
dialogue.defeat: Well, that wasn't my favorite ending. But nobody leaves a good show after one act.
dialogue.draw: Nobody wins! See, that is funny. Not to you? Tough crowd.
dialogue.rematch: Oh, absolutely. I've saved the strangest joke for the encore.

profiles.canon_background: The Joker is Batman's theatrical, unpredictable arch-enemy, best known for schemes that turn ordinary situations into dangerous spectacles. Interpretations vary across comics, films, and animation.
profiles.tempo_assessment: Filed a formal complaint because chess has rules. Filed a second complaint because Batman follows them.
profiles.character_interpretation: Gotham's theatrical criminal is interested in disrupting expectations rather than winning efficiently. On a chessboard, his chaos is calculated enough to be dangerous.
profiles.on_board_personality: Unusual move orders, practical traps, wild but sometimes sound sacrifices, and confusing complications.
profiles.voice_direction: Unsettling whimsy, PG dark humor, no violence or direct quotations.
profiles.running_bit_description: Joker insists this is a comedy show, then becomes annoyed when Batman's imagined criticism enters his own performance.

dialogue_arcs.theme: Joker insists this is a comedy show, then becomes annoyed when Batman's imagined criticism enters his own performance.

beats.line: The funny thing about Batman is he insists there's always a plan.
Now, if I make a plan, am I becoming Batman? Distressing thought.
Never mind. I lost the plan. Gotham's safe from that particular nightmare.

greeting.label: On initial game introduction
greeting.guard: start of match, before first move

quiet_move.label: After a quiet bot move
quiet_move.guard: legal bot move that was not capture, check or major tactic

capture_pawn.label: After bot captures a pawn
capture_pawn.guard: move captured enemy pawn; no terminal result

capture_major.label: After bot captures a rook or queen
capture_major.guard: captured enemy rook or queen; not king

opponent_blunder.label: After human blunder
opponent_blunder.guard: engine-confirmed material/position loss; do not use without analysis

own_blunder.label: After bot blunder
own_blunder.guard: engine-confirmed bot blunder; do not use without analysis

check.label: After bot gives check
check.guard: opponent king checked on committed move

in_check.label: After bot is checked
in_check.guard: human just checked the bot king

tactical_success.label: After confirmed motif
tactical_success.guard: legal bot move creates a real fork, pin, or other verified tactic

queen_lost.label: After bot queen is captured
queen_lost.guard: opponent just captured the bot queen; do not confuse sides

player_thinking.label: If human takes a long time
player_thinking.guard: human has spent >25 seconds on the move; at most once per game

rematch.label: Actual rematch
rematch.guard: player clicked rematch after finished game

voice_pack.cadence: one remark at most per turn; results > check > queen lost > verified tactics > capture > ordinary; optional speech and per-character cooldown; no fabricated chess claims
voice_pack.arc_hint_semantics: Designer hints only; a suggested trigger must be implemented and verified in the game before its line can fire. Never use arc beats as unconditional move-number jokes.
